evalplus.note: Dataset versions and the URL shape come from evalplus/data/humaneval.py (HUMANEVAL_PLUS_VERSION), evalplus/data/mbpp.py (MBPP_PLUS_VERSION) and evalplus/data/utils.py (get_dataset_metadata) at this commit. Grading rules are ported from evalplus/eval/__init__.py and evalplus/eval/_special_oracle.py at the same commit.

checksumProvenance: The EvalPlus dataset releases publish no checksums, and EvalPlus itself only hashes the file after download (data/humaneval.py::get_human_eval_plus_hash computes an md5 of the decompressed jsonl at runtime). The sha256 values below were computed from the first download on 2026-09-29 and are pinned here so later downloads are verified against them. Independent cross-checks: the record counts match the EvalPlus README (HumanEval+ 164 tasks; MBPP+ v0.2.0 '399 -> 378 tasks'), and the gzip byte sizes match the sizes reported by the GitHub releases API.

fixture.note: Three synthetic tasks in the HumanEval+ record shape. Not a benchmark: it exists so the loaders, the sandbox path, the replay backend, and the summarizer can be tested end to end without the real datasets. Generated by tests/fixtures/make_fixture.py.

java8-idioms.note: Authored in this repository: 8 categories x 3 tasks, each shipping task.json, prompt.java (the skeleton the model sees), Solution.java (the canonical answer) and Main.java (hidden tests using the shared Check helper). Not a standardized benchmark; it is the Java 8 idiom signal that HumanEval-X Java cannot give. Expected values are literals, computed by hand or in Python and reviewed, never copied from a model.

humanevalX.note: Formerly THUDM/humaneval-x. Only the Java split is used. Fields verified against the file at this revision: task_id, prompt, declaration, canonical_solution, test, example_test, text. The dataset publishes no checksum, so the sha256 below is the first-download hash, pinned here; the record count (164) matches HumanEval.
